result: In 260 blinded-assessed subjects, 4.4-year cumulative incidence of MCI (NACC/NIA-AA criteria) was 27% in long COVID vs 5% recovered and 1% COVID-negative (HR 3.93, 95% CI 1.86-8.31), mostly AD-type MCI.
reason: Long COVID version of objectively assessed cognitive impairment; clinical MCI diagnosis rather than domain-specific test scores, so extends rather than replicates.

result: ME/CFS patients meeting PEM criteria split into physical, mental, both and neither severe-PEM groups by questionnaire; the both group had the worst symptoms and function, and the neither group was still more disabled than controls (no numbers given).
reason: Measures self-reported PEM symptom-type subgroups, not PEM onset delay or recovery duration; manifestations, not non-physical triggers, so no atlas finding fits.

result: In German insurance data on 6,077 people aged 6-27 with ME/CFS matched 1:5 to controls, 44 ICD-10 code classes from the previous year raised the odds of a later ME/CFS diagnosis, including fatigue, depression, pain and somatoform disorders (OR 1.11-2.19), fibromyalgia (OR 2.08), MCI (OR 2.93) and post-COVID condition (OR 3.84, 2.97-4.98).
reason: Epidemiology/registry domain: diagnoses that come before a pediatric/young-adult ME/CFS diagnosis; the atlas registry finding covers only viral vs bacterial infection codes in Finnish adults.

result: 102 PCS vs 204 matched controls: lower venular flicker dilation (3.7% vs 4.5%), narrower arterioles (CRAE 178.3 vs 183.3 um) and lower AVR (0.83 vs 0.86); ME/CFS (n=62) most affected; IL-6, ICAM-1 and VCAM-1 raised.
reason: already cited: preprint of the All Eyes on PCS study (Wallraven 2026, BMC Med), same cohort and values.

result: In 119 participants (36 controls, 33 long COVID fatigue, 50 MS), a lower frontal (not occipital) resting EEG aperiodic exponent tracked cognitive fatigue and predicted fatigue status beyond age and depression, with good sensitivity and specificity.
reason: Resting quantitative EEG spectral measure with classification in a long COVID fatigue group; adds a specific aperiodic/E-I marker and a transdiagnostic comparison.

result: Whole-brain 31P-MRSI at 3T in 27 post-COVID patients vs 23 recovered controls showed lower ATP/PCr ratios across the cingulate cortex, with lower ACC ratios correlating with poorer MoCA/TMT-B; ME/CFS-criteria patients showed similar changes.
reason: Brain 31P energetics is covered by the newer neuro-31p-brain-energetics id; this adds a post-COVID cohort with an ME/CFS subgroup and links to cognition (claim text not in index, so check that it is not already cited).

result: A meta-analysis of 34 studies found a significant, large deficit in verbal working memory in ME/CFS vs controls but no significant difference in visual (object/spatial) working memory, and this held across span/attentional-control subtypes.
reason: Meta-analysis that probably overlaps in studies with Cockshell 2010, so not an independent replication; it refines the working-memory claim to verbal only, which makes it extends.

result: Among 208,050 Swedish women, more than 8 pre-pandemic symptom-based primary-care visits predicted later PCC (OR 5.45), PVFS (OR 7.71) and exhaustion disorder (OR 5.32) dose-dependently, though 17% of PCC cases had no such visits.
reason: Exposure is earlier symptom-based care-seeking, not prior viral vs bacterial infection; no atlas finding covers healthcare-use patterns before diagnosis.

result: In a 114-person randomised trial of 16 weeks of daily home taVNS vs sham vs placebo for post-COVID fatigue, only the adherent participants on active stimulation improved, with VAS fatigue 11.9 +/- 17.8 points better at 8 weeks (p=0.003, N=24).
reason: Treatments domain: no atlas trial finding covers vagus nerve stimulation; the positive result comes only from a per-protocol adherent subgroup.

result: Clinical WGS of 31 affected people from 25 families (RNA-seq in 16 affected, 7 unaffected) found pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in 8 of 25 probands (32%) and 12 of 31 affected (39%), across heterogeneous energy-metabolism, ion-homeostasis and synaptic genes.
reason: Same question of rare-variant contribution, using a family-based n-of-1 design; small, with no case-control comparison and no test of the HEAL2 genes.
